reasons: Lake record status is verified and identity matches United States v. Kenneth D. Gooch in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, decided 1993.
Lake citations list 6 F.3d 673 as the selected official citation and include the asserted parallel and vendor-neutral citations.
Lake treatment field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30, so the disclosed record does not show the cited authority is no longer live law.
residual_risks: Treatment audit risks are addressed under assertion c6390624462ca548.

reasons: Lens B does not attack support taxonomy unless a treatment/currency defect undermines it.
The page lists Gooch under Tents as Key — Anchor, and the disclosed treatment judgment does not finally downgrade the case.
residual_risks: Role strength was not independently reviewed for support under Lens B.

defect.problem: The holding embeds the authority label 'Persuasive (outside circuit) — 9th Cir.' even though the page/lake treatment metadata supports Binding in-circuit — 9th Cir. The substantive holding is not attacked under Lens B, but the weight parenthetical is inconsistent.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace the parenthetical with '(Binding in-circuit — 9th Cir.)' or remove weight labels from holding text.

reasons: Lake identity places the case in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit with circuit 9th.
The page's authority_weight field says Binding in-circuit — 9th Cir., conflicting with the holding's persuasive/outside-circuit label.
residual_risks: No support or quote-fidelity review performed.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep authority weight in the dedicated authority_weight field and avoid duplicating it inside holding prose.

reasons: Lake identity identifies Gooch as a Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals decision.
A Ninth Circuit court-of-appeals case supports the disclosed label Binding in-circuit — 9th Cir.; the lake record contains no final point override changing that weight label.
residual_risks: Binding effect is only in-circuit; outside the Ninth Circuit the case would be persuasive.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: For national users, display 'Binding in Ninth Circuit; persuasive elsewhere.'

defect.problem: The good_law field is present in the lake judgment fields, but the page's unqualified subsequent-history language is too strong because the disclosed lake treatment derivation has audit-needed, proposed negative-looking progeny edges.
defect.proposed_fix: Keep good_law only with an audit caveat, and remove or qualify 'No negative subsequent treatment identified' until the R15 treatment audit is completed.

reasons: Lake treatment.field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30, and point_overrides is empty, so the core good-law call survives from disclosed judgment fields.
But lake treatment.edges include proposed questioned, criticized, overruled, abrogated, and superseded_by_statute labels, and lane2_top_cited has audit_needed true with proposed_negative_events 24.
Because those edges are proposed and field_iii is mentioned, they do not prove Gooch is overruled; they do defeat an uncaveated 'No negative subsequent treatment identified' presentation.
residual_risks: as_of_content 1993-09-23 predates the lake identity date_decided 1993-10-06; disclosed records do not explain the legacy metadata semantics.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Display treatment as 'good_law per migrated judgment field; R15 progeny audit pending' until proposed edges are resolved.
